answers.falsifier: A launch with claude absent installs it or exits 127 loudly; --dry-run installs nothing; on Windows the PowerShell installer is the one invoked; with the install branch of superclaude.py removed the proof reds.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a sibling of c3cd232ba0cf (CairnCommons/tickets/c3cd232ba0cf-*.json) raised by the orchestrator on 2026-11-23 from Akien's 2026-11-11 ruling quoted at cairn/devices/cc/superclaude:461
answers.how: One new proof drives main() of superclaude.py through its seams (which, install, out, err) with claude absent: dry-run says what it would install and installs nothing, a real launch calls the installer with the default or CAIRN_CLAUDE_INSTALLER url after looking in ~/.local/bin, a failed install exits 127 loudly, and the real installer picks curl|sh or the PowerShell installer by the launch tool's answer.
answers.traces_to: Akien's 2026-11-11 ruling 'if claude is not installed, it should be' (cairn/devices/cc/superclaude:461); Law 3 and Law 8 (code with no tooth is a hypothesis, and a hollow build must not pass); outline 10.3.2.1.
answers.what: superclaude.py installs Claude Code when it is absent, and a proof measures the install path on Windows and Linux, so retiring the bash drops no ruling.
